title: A good Mirecourt Violin by Louis GENIN Luthier bearing the maker's label Luthier Moderne, dated 1904, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (359mm), in case. The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain widening to the flanks, the transparent varnish of a red-brown colour on a yellow ground.

A Mirecourt Violin, circa 1920, labelled Jean Morlot Luthier, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (359mm), with a bow in case. The two-piece back of narrow curl, the table of broad grain, the transparent varnish of an orange-red colour on a yellow ground.

An attractive Violin by Rushworth & Dreaper in Liverpool dated 1930, The Apollo Violin, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (359mm), with a bow in case. The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of narrow curl, the table of narrow grain, the transparent varnish of an orange colour on a yellow ground (12 very minute pin hole marks in the back).

A Violin by C. F. Larsen in Odense branded on the inner back and dated 1861, no. M174, L.O.B. 14in. (355mm). The one-piece, ribs and scroll of narrow curl, table of broad grain, varnish of a light brown colour. Minus tailpiece and top nut.

A good Violin by O. Lyngaas Christiania in Norway bearing the maker's label dated 1916, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (359mm). The attractive two-piece back of narrow flame, ribs and scroll of similar figure, table of narrow grain, varnish of a clear orange colour on a yellow ground. Good condition.  Medals awarded in Paris, Bergen and Stockholm.

A Violin by D. Nicolas Ainé bearing the maker's brand on the inner back, circa 1790, L.O.B. 14 3/16in. (360mm). The attractive one-piece back of horizontal, narrow curl, ribs and scroll of similar figure, the one-piece table of medium grain, varnish of a clear red-brown colour. Table off, minus tailpiece.
A Saxon Viola, circa 1880, L.O.B. 15 5/16in. (389mm). The two-piece back and ribs of narrow figure, scroll plain, table of broad grain, varnish of a brown colour. Good condition.

A French Violin, circa 1800 of the Maucotel School bearing a repair label dated 1856, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (359mm). The two-piece back of matched narrow curl, the ribs of less figure, the scroll plain, the table of medium grain widening to broad on the flanks, the varnish of a golden-brown colour, the inner flanks red.

A good Paris School Violin, circa 1890 labelled Joseph Guarnerius, L.O.B. 14in. (354mm), with a nickel mounted French violin bow in shaped case. The two-piece back of medium flame ascending from the joint, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain, the varnish of a red-brown colour on a light brown ground.

A Violin by John W. Owen bearing the maker's label in Leeds dated 1928 and inscribed on the inner back no. 143, L.O.B. 14 1/16in. (357mm), with two bows in case. The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of narrow curl, the table of broad slightly wavy grain, the varnish of a red-brown colour on a yellow ground with some over varnish on the table and scroll.

A French Petite Viola, circa 1910, L.O.B. 14 1/2in. (367mm), with a bow, case and cover. The two-piece back, ribs and scroll of bird's-eye figure, the table of medium grain, the transparent varnish of an orange colour. Good condition.

A Violin bearing the label Ferdinandus Aug HOMOLKA fecit Pragae 1860 and labelled Antonius Stradivarius, L.O.B. 14 1/16in. (357mm). The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of open broad grain, the varnish of a red colour on a light brown ground. Minus tailpiece.

A Violin by James Hardie & Sons bearing the maker's label in Edinburgh dated 1900, L.O.B. 14 3/16in. (360mm), with a bow in a shaped brown leather case. The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain, the varnish of a golden brown colour. Double purfled.

An interesting Violin, circa 1780 labelled Nicolaus Amatius, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (359mm), in case. The two-piece back cut on the slab without figure, the ribs and scroll of similar wood, the table of strong medium grain, the varnish of a red-brown colour.

A good Violin of the Heberlein School, circa 1900, L.O.B. 14 1/16in. (357mm), with two bows, one repaired silver mounted bow, in case. The two-piece back of medium flame, ribs and scroll of narrow curl, table of narrow grain, varnish of a red colour on an orange golden brown ground. Good condition.

A good German Viola of the Munich School, circa 1950 labelled Paolo Fiorini Taurini, L.O.B. 16 1/8in. (409mm), in case. The one-piece back, ribs and scroll of narrow curl, table of narrow grain widening to medium, the transparent varnish of an orange-red colour on a yellow ground. Mint condition.
A silver mounted Viola Bow by L. Cocker stamped on the shaft. The ebony frog with pearl eyes, the octagonal canewood stick, head and shaft of pernambuco, 60gms.

A Violin by William Old bearing the maker's label in Falmouth dated 1897, L.O.B. 14 3/8in. (365mm), in case. The two-piece back plain, ribs of narrow grain, varnish of a light golden brown colour. Good condition.

A good Violin by Williamson Blyth bearing the maker's manuscript label in Edinburgh dated 1890, L.O.B. 14 3/8in. (365mm), in case. The two-piece back, ribs and scroll of narrow curl, table of narrow grain, varnish of an orange-red colour on a yellow ground. Seven-ply purfling.

A Violin attributed to Georg Kloz in Mittenwald, circa 1770, labelled Nicolaus Amatius, L.O.B. 13 7/8in. (353mm), with a bow in case. (A small patch in the make bottom left back.)  With a receipt of Messrs J. & H. Beare, London, dated May 1962 for a Violin of the Kloz School.

A Violin by Eugene Marchand bearing a manuscript label Paris Novembre 1891, L.O.B. 14 1/16in. (357mm), in case. The two-piece back of narrow flame descending from the joint, the ribs and scroll of similar figure, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a red-brown colour on a yellow ground.

A French Violin bearing the maker's label G. CERPI Lutherie Artistique and dated 1897, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (359mm). The two-piece back of brilliant medium flame, the ribs of narrow curl, the scroll of medium curl, the table of even medium grain, the transparent varnish of an orange colour.

A Violin by Jean Baptiste Colin bearing the maker's label Lutherie Artistique annee 1886, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (359mm). The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain widening to the flanks, the varnish of a clear orange red-brown colour.

A good French Violin, circa 1880 labelled Copie Maginni, L.O.B. 14 3/8in. (365mm). The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain widening to medium, the varnish of an orange-brown colour.

A Violin by Louis Lowendall bearing the maker's label in Dresden, circa 1880 and branded Berlin below the button, L.O.B. 14 1/16in. (357mm). A French Violin, circa 1870, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (359mm). The two-piece back of medium flame descending from the joint, the ribs and scroll of varied curl, the table of broad grain, the varnish of an orange-red colour on a yellow ground.

A Violin of the Schlosser in Klingenthal School, circa 1800, bearing repair labels, L.O.B. 14 1/8in. (359mm). The two-piece back of narrow figure, the ribs of similar curl, the scroll plain, the table of narrow grain, the transparent varnish of a golden brown colour, minus tailpiece.

A Violin by Neuner & Hornsteiner in Mittenwald, circa 1870 bearing the maker's label, L.O.B. 13 7/8in. (353mm). The two-piece back of narrow figure, the ribs similar, the scroll plain, the table of narrow grain, the varnish of a chestnut red-brown colour. Minus tailpiece.

A Violin by J. PRIESTNALL in Rochdale, dated 1888, branded on the interior and upper and lower back, no. 70, L.O.B. 14 1/4in. (362mm). The two-piece back, ribs and scroll showing narrow figure, the table of open broad grain, the varnish of a brown colour on a yellow ground. Fine condition.

A Violin by OTTO SEIFERT and Dr. Grossman bearing the label dated 1908 with a signature and NEV CREMONA, L.O.B. 14in. (255mm). The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of strong medium grain, the clear varnish of a golden brown colour.

A Violin, circa 1700 of the Bolzano School labelled MATTHIAS ALBANI anno 1674, L.O.B. 14in. (355mm).
